sections.h2: Where is Leawood, Kansas, and how is it shaped?
sections.html:
Leawood is a Johnson County suburb in the southwest corner of the Kansas City area, and it is long and narrow. The Census Bureau lists 15.16 square miles, stretching more than 9 miles north to south and about 2 miles east to west.

Its eastern edge is the Kansas-Missouri state line, where it meets eight Kansas City, Missouri neighborhoods. Prairie Village borders it on the north and northwest, and Overland Park on the west and south. The city is divided into four wards, and Wikipedia reports that about 75 percent of its land is developed. That figure means most Leawood houses are already built, and sellers compete with other resale homes more than with new lots.

The population history shows a city that has largely filled in. Census counts were 27,656 in 2000, 31,867 in 2010 and 33,902 in 2020, and the 6.4 percent growth in the last decade was the slowest of any decade in the census table. As of 2015, Wikipedia describes Leawood as one of the wealthiest suburbs in the Kansas City area, citing the Hallbrook and Mission Hill Estates neighborhoods as examples. Houses in that bracket are often expected to be in showing condition, and bringing an older house up to that level is where many sellers lose time.

sections.h2: How did Leawood start, and why do deed restrictions matter?
sections.html:
Modern Leawood began in the 1920s, when Oscar G. Lee moved to Johnson County and oversaw the building of Lee Boulevard. The city is named for him. A housing development by the Kroh Brothers led to incorporation on November 30, 1948, when Leawood was a third-class city with fewer than 2,000 people. It became a second-class city by 1959 and a first-class city by 2014.

The Kroh Brothers modeled their neighborhoods on those of Kansas City developer J. C. Nichols, who used curving streets, uniform architecture, extensive deed restrictions and homes associations. That heritage explains why so many Leawood subdivisions still sit under recorded covenants. When you sell, those covenants and the association's rules travel with the house, and a buyer or a title company will want them.

sections.h2: Who runs the neighborhood rules in Leawood?
sections.html:
Most Leawood neighborhoods have homeowners associations, so the city's rules and the association's rules both apply. The city's Neighborhood Services office enforces a Property Maintenance Code covering premise condition, paint, roof overhangs, gutters and exterior structure condition.

Leawood's residential code also lets a legally constituted homes association file a written request with the city's Building Official, so an association can have a formal role when exterior work is proposed. A seller planning repairs before listing should check both sides first.

  • Call Leawood code staff before replacing a roof, fence or exterior features.
  • Ask the association whether the work needs architectural approval.
  • Get dues, transfer fees and any open assessments in writing for the buyer.
  • Confirm whether the house is in a single association or in more than one overlapping group.

Skipping these steps is a common reason a conventional closing slips. A cash sale avoids most of the pre-listing work, although the association may still need a transfer notice.

sections.h2: What do major employers say about Leawood's economy?
sections.html:
Leawood is a professional-services and office suburb more than an industrial one. The city's 2017 annual financial report, summarized on Wikipedia, listed these top employers.

City of Leawood256

Wikipedia notes that Select Quote cut to fewer than 50 local staff after 2024 layoffs, so employer lists change. The city also has Town Center Plaza, a shopping center with upscale retailers. Because Leawood's economy depends on office work and a short commute to the rest of the metro, a house here may draw buyers moving for a job in the Kansas City area.

Two public districts serve Leawood: Blue Valley USD 229 and the Shawnee Mission School District. Which one a house belongs to depends on its address, and families ask about it early, so put the correct district in your listing or sales notes.

The Johnson County Library serves Leawood residents. The Leawood Police Department was formed on January 18, 1949, and has about 60 officers today, with help from the Johnson County Sheriff's Office.

sections.h2: How does Johnson County tax a Leawood home?
sections.html:
Johnson County bills and collects real estate tax for Leawood, and the County Clerk sets mill levies for each local taxing authority. A mill is 1/1000 of a dollar, so one mill on $1,000 of assessed value is $1.00 in tax.

The county appraiser's calendar sets the rhythm of the year:

DateWhat happens
January 1Valuation date for the appraisal roll
On or before March 1Notices of Appraised Value mailed
On or before March 31Appeal deadline, 30 days from mailing the notice
November 15Tax bills mailed to owners
December 20First half or full tax payment due

For residential property, a portion of assessed value is exempt from the 20-mill school general levy. The county lists 8,625 of assessed value exempt for tax years 2024 and 2025, a credit of $172.50. If you sell in spring, ask the title company how it will split the year's bill, because Kansas taxes are paid in arrears.

sections.h2: How are deeds recorded for a Leawood sale?
sections.html:
Leawood deeds go to the Johnson County Register of Deeds at 111 S. Cherry Street, Suite 1200, in Olathe. The office records documents over the counter on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and by mail, and it cannot take a document by email or fax.

The county's fee for recording a deed is $21.00 for the first page and $17.00 for each additional page, set by K.S.A. 28-115. Electronic recording is available through an approved vendor, which is how title companies usually file. If you need to add a beneficiary to a house you own, a Transfer on Death deed must be signed and notarized before recording and carries the same page fees.

sections.h2: What are the options for selling a Leawood house?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell privately or take a cash offer. In an established suburb with association rules, the main differences are time, repairs and certainty.

  • A listing may suit a well-kept house when you can prepare it and wait.
  • A private sale saves a fee but leaves the paperwork and association documents to you.
  • A cash purchase suits an inherited house, a divorce, a relocation or a property that needs updating.

We buy houses in Leawood as-is. If you want to compare, request an offer and set it beside the net from a listing after repairs, dues, taxes and carrying costs.

faqs.q: Do Leawood homeowners associations affect a sale?
faqs.a: Yes. Most Leawood neighborhoods have associations, so dues, transfer fees and covenants usually need to be disclosed to the buyer. Ask the association for a current statement early, and check whether more than one group covers your address.

faqs.q: When are Johnson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half or full amount is due on or before December 20. Johnson County mails real estate tax bills around November 15, and the appraiser mails valuation notices on or before March 1.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Leawood property valuation?
faqs.a: The deadline is 30 days after the Notice of Appraised Value is mailed, which is on or before March 31 in the county's calendar.

faqs.q: Which school district is Leawood in?
faqs.a: Leawood is served by two public districts, Blue Valley USD 229 and the Shawnee Mission School District. Which one applies depends on the street address.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Leawood house in an association without making repairs first?
faqs.a: A cash buyer purchases as-is, so cosmetic or deferred repairs do not need to be done before closing. Association dues, transfer fees and any open violation notices from the city still need to be disclosed and settled through the title company.

faqs.q: Where is a Leawood deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Johnson County Register of Deeds in Olathe, at 111 S. Cherry Street, Suite 1200. A title company normally records it electronically for you.
